name: OSWorld
description: Operate real desktop applications and verify the resulting operating-system or application state.
input: Natural-language instruction and initialized desktop environment
output: Desktop actions that change applications or files
assessment: Task-specific execution checks on the resulting state
date_note: Existing entry and stable slug; bare family labels need source context before assigning an edition result.

name: SWE-bench
description: Modify a real Python repository to resolve a GitHub issue; regression tests judge the patch.
input: Repository snapshot and corresponding GitHub issue
assessment: Required issue-fixing and regression tests must pass
date_note: Existing entry and stable slug; bare family labels need source context before assigning an edition result.

name: SWE-bench Verified
description: Run the SWE-bench repair task on a human-validated subset of 500 issues.
input: Human-validated issue and matching repository snapshot
assessment: Same test-based resolution criterion, on 500 validated issues
date_note: Existing entry and stable slug; bare family labels need source context before assigning an edition result.

name: OSWorld-Verified
description: The maintainers corrected task definitions, starting states and evaluators in the original computer-use benchmark. This named release is not an arbitrary verified submission.
input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
output: Actions that change application or system state
assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.

name: OSWorld 2.0
description: A new long-horizon suite in realistic desktop environments. The first public V2 release pinned its task, asset and environment snapshots.
input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
output: Actions that change application or system state
assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.
date_note: Maintainer README explicitly announces launch June 26. The initial snapshot is named 2026.06.24; its name is not the announcement date. Untimed OSWorld 2.0 results do not identify which later snapshot was used.

name: OSWorld 2.0 (2026.08.08)
description: The August 2.0 snapshot revises task evaluators and website assets. The release notes identify both task hardening and fairness fixes; the VM images remain from June.
input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
output: Actions that change application or system state
assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.

name: OSWorld 2.1
description: A named release with revised tasks, task assets, evaluation workflows and mocked websites. Frozen component versions define the score’s environment.
input: Desktop observation and a task instruction
output: Actions that change application or system state
assessment: Task-specific executable checks validate the resulting state; report task set, snapshot and action budget.
date_note: Retain the offline-set or partial-set qualifier; those do not mean a full-suite result.

name: SWE-bench Lite
description: A 300-task test subset selected for cost-effective evaluation on self-contained repository issues.
input: An issue description and its repository snapshot
assessment: Fraction of selected issues resolved by the test harness.
date_note: The project dates Lite to March 2024; this is the author’s dated full dataset upload, not an empty repository creation event.

name: SWE-bench Multimodal
description: The initial multimodal software engineering release uses 517 issues with visual evidence from JavaScript projects.
input: A repository, issue description and associated visual evidence
assessment: Fraction of issues resolved on the original evaluation split.
date_note: Original paper v1. An unversioned result reported after September 1, 2026 does not by itself establish use of the v2 test split.

name: SWE-bench Multimodal V2
description: The V2 edition keeps 480 reproducible issues, drops flaky or ungradeable tests, and publishes its full test split and tooling.
input: A repository, issue description and associated visual evidence
assessment: Fraction of the V2 issues resolved, using the revised visual-asset and JavaScript evaluation pipeline.

name: SWE-bench Multilingual
description: Evaluate repository patches on 300 tasks drawn from 42 repositories in nine programming languages. It is not Multi-SWE-bench.
input: An issue description and project files in the task’s programming language
assessment: Fraction of instances passing the task’s repository tests.
date_note: First substantive maintainer dataset upload located. “Multilingual” refers to programming languages, not translations of the same prompts.

name: SWE-Bench Pro
description: Scale’s independently produced suite tests long-horizon engineering work. Public, held-out and commercial splits are not interchangeable.
input: A repository snapshot and engineering requirement
assessment: Task resolution under the specified split and repository test harness.
date_note: Scale’s Pro suite is distinct from the original Princeton-led dataset. Preserve public/held-out qualifiers; unsuffixed later reports need version evidence.

name: SWE-Bench Pro V2
description: Scale refreshes the public Pro split and its execution protocol, including validated checks and network-restricted evaluation.
input: A repository snapshot and Pro V2 task specification
assessment: Task resolution on the V2 public split under its published run protocol.

name: LiveCodeBench v1
description: The cumulative code-generation snapshot contains 400 problems from May 2023 through Mar 2024. A narrower contest-date filter selects a different evaluation.
input: A contest problem statement and examples
assessment: Pass@1 or reported pass@k on the specified snapshot and problem-date window.
date_note: Original public paper and substantive data upload share March 12 UTC.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: Publisher dataset commit identifying the edition.
